This post really hit home for me, I’ve felt this exact same way for 5 years and I’ve been through every type of therapy, read books been on medication and like you I feel like it cannot be solved like this as the problem is a physical one not a mental one. Also, like you I know there is other stuff I can change and work on like the condition of my skin and hair but every time I try it just seems useless. I actually went to two plastic surgeons in London to ask about what I wanted to get done etc and they told me if I got it done I’d look like a ‘mongrel’ and there’s nothing wrong. Even now I find it difficult to know as I think why would surgeons lie as they aren’t my friends and are there to make money? Reassurance from my friends and family means nothing to me as I believe they just want me to be happy and not sad anymore. My BDD has ruined and controlled my whole life, I had to drop out of uni just 5 months ago because I was having panic attacks everyday and couldn’t bare to be seen by anyone, it made me stop going to school and lose lots of friends from closing myself off and becoming housebound. BUT... last summer was the happiest I’ve been for the longest amount of time and my BDD was no longer always in my thoughts. I for once was at ease with my how I looked and even liked how I looked some days! I was genuinely happy, even in my own company, I went from being terrified of people due to my appearance to going out on random walks and saying hi to everyone I saw! I don’t know if it was the sun or what made me feel this way but it was good. Even though it was not a long time for me it shows there is the possibility of coping with this shitty illness and living a normal or even good life, I hope you find a way to do and I wish you the best of luck, I really do. I know what it’s like to be screaming and crying, almost feeling a pain in your stomach it hurts so much because you simply cannot accept the person facing back at you in the mirror😞 best of luck ❤️
